verdict.rationale: a-Shell ships its own programmatic surfaces: Apple Shortcuts actions (Execute Command, Put File, Get File) and an optional built-in HTTPS relay whose POST /run accepts any command line. Because nearly all UI functionality is itself exposed as shell commands (including config), much of the UI is reachable programmatically. However, parity with the UI is never documented, the relay is off by default and meant for trusted networks, and Shortcuts runs are noted as not always working. Some features are inherently interactive pickers (pickFolder, the font picker). missing for 10: documented UI/API parity, a formal API spec or OpenAPI, programmatic equivalents for picker-based UI actions (pickFolder, font picker), API versioning/changelog, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: a-Shell is compatible with Apple Shortcuts, giving users full control of the Shell.
`Execute Command`, which takes a list of commands and executes them in order.
POST /run takes a UTF-8 command line as its body and requires Content-Length and X-Token
You can force a specific shortcut to run "in App" or "in Extension", with the warning that it won't always work.
